take_homes: Agent risk is mostly about what it can read and change, so the cheapest control is not connecting it, and that costs a feature.
The audit gives rows I can check (compliant / violating / can't tell), and whoever owns the area takes the 'can't tell' rows. That is a process I can defend.
One risk fixed is a prototype; every risk fixed is production. That work has a cost nobody gave me.

monday.move: Ask IT and legal which of the 'can't tell' policy rows they own before my controller touches any finance data with an agent.
monday.stop_condition: IT says no finance data in the tool until a review is done.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data; I also have no cost per month for 40 people.

misconception.why: A licence does not decide what the agent can reach or who signs for the residual risk. The organisation has to scope it, check it and sign. That is a capability, not a purchase. Still no price, so I only half believe it.

one_line: The middle forty minutes were useful because the audit gave me rows I could check; the filler paragraphs and the missing cost per month were not.
